attach-one now reconnects by itself (branch fix/attach-reconnect, worktree /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-attach-reconnect, commit 50a898a). The targeted tests pass (43), and each of the 9 new tests fails against the original code.

The change is in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-attach-reconnect/workflow/interactive.py. attach-one now runs `claude attach <id>` as a child process with cwd set to the worktree, instead of exec'ing it. That way it survives the attach and can work out what happened from the run's own records and the session list.

How I told a detach from a lost connection: I read the attach code bundled in Claude Code 2.1.281 (static reading only) and ran `claude attach deadbeef` (exit 1, "No job matching", no session started). A detach (Ctrl+Z, or ← to the agent view) and "Session <id> has exited" both end with exit 0. "Couldn't reconnect to <id> — background service is unavailable" and every other error end with exit 1. An attach to a session that is no longer running wakes it again, which is the implicit restart the refusal guards against. Claude's Ctrl+Z handler signals the whole process group, so running attach as a child keeps Ctrl+Z working.

What happens after each attach, in this order:
- **(c) Stopped by the controller.** If `<node>.stop.json` exists, confirmed or not, it prints once `Worker <lane> was stopped by the controller at <time> (<reason>); nothing to attach.` and exits 0. The time and reason come from the matching stop event in events.jsonl; after a blocked worker wait the reason is "the run blocked: ...". Reviewers get `Reviewer <id> ...`. If the stop is already recorded, nothing is listed and nothing is attached.
- **(a) Operator detach.** Exit 0 with the session alive: it exits quietly. An attach the operator interrupted (exit 130, or killed by SIGINT) is treated the same way.
- **(b) Lost connection.** A non-zero exit (or the CLI missing mid-update) while the exact session is still alive and not stopped prints `Lost the connection to <lane> (<id>); the background service may be restarting. Reattaching in Ns…` and reattaches the same id. Delays go 2, 4, 8, then 10 s, and it gives up after 30 attempts in a row with a clear message. An attach that held for 60 s starts a new count. If the service briefly cannot confirm the session (no CLI, empty listing, row still registering its PID) while the attached process lives, it waits within the same limit.
- **(d) Gone without a recorded stop.** It prints the existing refusal once and exits 1. It never restarts a session.

Ctrl+C exits with 130, a one-line message and no traceback.

The end-to-end smoke run found one bug, now fixed. A session that has exited but not yet been cleaned up by its parent (a zombie) still passes the `kill(pid, 0)` check, so attach-one printed a misleading "Reattaching" line before refusing, and could even have attached to an ended session. attach-one now treats a zombie as gone (it reads `/proc/<pid>/stat`), and the test reproduces this case.

Smoke runs, all with a fake `claude` first on PATH:
- the live run directory, read-only: stop message for ui and controller, exit 0, directory unchanged, no claude call;
- a scratch run from `prepare()`: lost connection then reattach, and a vanished session refused once;
- a real Ctrl+C through a pseudo-terminal during the backoff: exit 130.

The Herdr pane command in attach_pane is unchanged and needs no shell loop. RUNBOOK section 3 and the command-reference note now describe this behaviour and say not to wrap attach-one in a loop.

One slip during the red phase: the second red run of the new tests against the old code reached the unpatched `os.execvp` and exec'd a real `claude attach 11111111` (possibly twice). It only printed "No job matching '11111111'" and exited; no session exists with that id and none was started. After that I checked the red phase with execvp and chdir replaced by stubs.

It now follows the run's events.jsonl through a new `Timeline` context manager. The terminal gets a header (`Supervising <run>; timeline in UTC, the last 5 of N events:` or `no events yet.`), then the last 5 events, then one line per new event as `HH:MM:SS  node  status  message`, in UTC and flushed at once. The children and other commands write the file, so a thread reads it once a second from a byte offset. A line only counts once its newline is written, and sequence numbers stop any event printing twice across controller restarts; a file that got shorter is read again from the start, skipping what was shown. problems.description: observe() decides whether a failure while the attached PID lives is transient from the exception type and message. Listing failures count only as OSError, ValueError or SubprocessError, plus RuntimeErrors whose text starts with one of TRANSIENT_REFUSALS. The sibling branch fix/autoupdate (commits 8c6d1e1 and 016635b, which own inventory() and run_claude) changes inventory() to raise TransientInfraError(RuntimeError) with the message 'Claude session inventory unavailable: ...'. It does this for timeouts, a non-zero exit, unparseable output, and ENOENT/ENOEXEC once its 60 s grace runs out. After the integrator merges both branches, observe() re-raises exactly the failure a background-service restart produces, and attach-one exits 1 'Blocked: Claude session inventory unavailable'. That is the dead pane this branch was meant to fix. The new tests cannot catch it, because they fake inventory() failures with FileNotFoundError, which stays an OSError after the merge.
problems.failure_scenario: The branches are merged. A Claude Code reinstall restarts the service, `claude attach` exits 1 ('Couldn't reconnect … background service is unavailable'), and the next `claude agents --json` exits non-zero while the service comes back. inventory() then raises TransientInfraError('Claude session inventory unavailable: …'). observe() lands in `except RuntimeError`, the message matches no TRANSIENT_REFUSALS prefix, and the error is re-raised. attach-one exits 1 and the pane is dead again. I reproduced this in a scratch probe that subclasses AttachOneTests and has inventory() raise a RuntimeError subclass with that message: attach_one raises instead of reattaching.
problems.fix: In observe(), call `rows = sessions.inventory()` in its own try block. While `waiting` is true, treat any Exception from the listing as a gap to wait out, still bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT. This is safe because nothing is attached without a verified live row. Keep the prefix matching only for locate()'s refusals ('No live native PID', 'Session is not attachable'). Add a test in which inventory() raises a RuntimeError subclass with an unrelated message mid-restart and the pane still reattaches. Two notes for the merge: the attach subprocess.run should receive the sibling's claude_env() (DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1), because a `claude attach` client is a long-lived Claude Code process in every pane. The sibling's test_attach_one_waits_out_a_claude_update_with_the_auto_updater_off patches os.execvp and must be rewritten for the subprocess-based attach.

problems.description: In the real freeze, stop_session writes `<node>.stop.json` with stopped:false, runs `claude stop`, and only then saves stopped:true. The freeze event is written after every worker is confirmed. The attached pane's `claude attach` exits at `claude stop`, so the recorded_stop check that follows almost always finds the marker unconfirmed. A live pane therefore prints 'Worker ui was stopped by the controller at … (stop requested, not yet confirmed); nothing to attach.', never the freeze reason. My end-to-end pty run with a fake claude showed exactly this line. The unit test test_a_stop_recorded_by_the_controller_ends_attach_one_without_a_reattach writes a confirmed marker and the freeze event during the attach, an order the controller never produces. The behaviour (exit 0, no reattach) is right in both cases; only the message and the realism of the test are off.
problems.failure_scenario: A live freeze with the panes attached: every worker pane shows '(stop requested, not yet confirmed)' rather than 'Native workers stopped before snapshot capture: …' or the blocked reason.
problems.fix: When the marker is unconfirmed, poll it briefly (for example up to the stop timeout of about 20 s) for stopped:true and the event before printing. Otherwise word that case as 'is being stopped by the controller (stop requested at <time>)'. Make the test write an unconfirmed marker during the attach, as the controller does.

problems.description: recorded_stop() is checked before observe(), and observe() runs `claude agents --json`, which can take seconds (up to its 15 s timeout) while the service restarts. A controller stop that writes its marker during that call is missed, and the attach goes ahead. `claude attach` wakes a job it finds gone ('Waking session …', seen in the CLI's attach code), so a stop that completes just before the attach probes would bring the stopped worker back. stop_workers would then block the run with 'A stopped worker was restarted'. The old code had the same window once per pane start. The reattach loop now opens it on every retry.
problems.failure_scenario: A pane is reattaching during a service restart when the freeze starts. attach-one finds no marker and starts a slow inventory call. The controller writes the marker and runs `claude stop`. attach-one's liveness check passes just before the process exits, and `claude attach` finds no job and wakes it.
problems.fix: Check recorded_stop() again immediately before subprocess.run(['claude', 'attach', …]), after observe() returns the row. The marker is written before `claude stop`, so a stop in progress is always seen and the window shrinks to microseconds.

problems.description: ATTACH_STABLE_SECONDS (60 s) is the same as the transient wait inside `claude attach` itself: wr() loops up to Oi = 60000 ms on ESTARTING/ERESPAWNING before it exits 1 with 'is restarting — try again in a moment'. An attach that never connected but spent its 60 s waiting counts as 'held', resets `failures` to 0 and sleeps 2 s. A service stuck in that state keeps attach-one retrying about once a minute indefinitely, and the documented 'gives up after 30 attempts in a row' never triggers.
problems.failure_scenario: The service keeps reporting ESTARTING for the job while `claude agents` still lists a live row. Every attach takes about 60 s and exits 1, `failures` resets each time, and the pane prints 'Lost the connection … Reattaching in 2s…' about once a minute with no end.
problems.fix: Set the threshold well above the CLI's own transient wait (for example 180–300 s). Otherwise count such attaches toward the limit and reset only when an attach clearly connected.

problems.description: recorded_stop() reads `<node>.stop.json` but never compares its recorded identity (background_id, session_id) with the node's current `<node>.interactive.json` receipt. Today a node is never relaunched in the same run directory, so this is latent. The lane-repair design now in progress (`relaunch <run> <lane>`, lane-repair-design.md) would rebind a frozen lane to a new session, and attach-one would then refuse to attach it, saying it was stopped.
problems.failure_scenario: A future lane repair relaunches `ui` under a new session while the old ui.stop.json remains. attach-one --node ui prints 'Worker ui was stopped by the controller …' and never attaches the live repaired session.
problems.fix: Count a marker only when its session_id (or background_id) matches the receipt's session_id or background_id. Otherwise ignore it as the stop of an earlier session.

problems.description: `except OSError: code = 1` around the attach is meant for a missing or half-written `claude` binary, but it also swallows cwd errors, for example a removed worktree or review-worktree raising FileNotFoundError with filename=<cwd>. Those become 'Lost the connection … the background service may be restarting' and up to 30 retries (about 4.5 min) before 'Gave up'. The old code failed at once with 'Blocked: [Errno 2] … <worktree>'.
problems.failure_scenario: The review-worktree or a lane worktree is removed while its session row is still listed. attach-one misreports a service restart and loops for minutes instead of naming the missing directory.
problems.fix: Treat the OSError as a lost connection only when error.filename is the executable (or errno is ENOENT, ENOEXEC or ETXTBSY for the executable). Re-raise anything else so main prints 'Blocked: …'.

problems.description: Waiting is allowed only while the previously attached PID lives. The installed CLI also has an upgrade-respawn path (ERESPAWNING, 'Agent is updating to the new Claude Code…', 'Job is respawning after an upgrade — try attach again in a moment'), in which the session process is replaced under the same job id and gets a new PID. If the row is still registering at that moment ('No live native PID' or state 'starting'), observe() raises immediately because the old PID is dead, and the pane dies even though the session lives. The case seen in workflow-guardrails-001 (sessions adopted with the same PID, 'claude.exe (deleted)') is handled correctly.
problems.failure_scenario: An update respawns the idle worker. `claude attach` exits 1 with 'Job is respawning after an upgrade'. The next listing shows the row without a PID, and attach-one exits 1 'Blocked: No live native PID; reconcile session before attaching'.
problems.fix: When the exact row (same id and sessionId) is listed but locate() refuses it with a transient refusal, wait even if the old PID has died. The wait stays bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT and never attaches without a verified live row.

A) After an edit, `resume` now commits the edited files and moves the run to that commit. The code is in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-challenge-resume/workflow/guardrails.py.
- `resume` without `--accept-challenge` first checks the edited task files and refuses one that lost a required heading. At that point nothing has been committed.
- The source checkout must be on the plan's `source_branch`. It refuses and lists any changed path other than the ones it re-pins (the lanes' task files, decisions.md and the PRD).
- It also refuses any commit after `base_commit` that it did not make. The message suggests `git reset --soft <base>` and a rerun.
- It then commits exactly the changed pinned paths. The message is `Workflow <run>: feature files revised after design challenge attempt <n>`, using the pipeline's own commit identity, with hooks and signing off.
- It then moves the run to that commit. Every worktree the repository has registered inside the run directory must be a clean checkout of the old base, or already at the new commit after an interrupted move. That means the lane worktrees and the challenge worktree. If any is not, it refuses before moving anything. Each worktree then runs `git checkout --detach` to the new commit, which avoids `git worktree add/remove`. plan.json then gets the new `base_commit` and each lane's `observed_start_commit`, as prepare sets them. The policy digest does not depend on the base. No receipt binds the plan digest before a worker launches, so none needs updating.
- After that it re-pins and reruns the challenge as before.
- Crash safety: a rerun recognises the commits `resume` made itself (by author, subject and paths) and carries on with no second commit. While a move is unfinished, `start` refuses because the challenge is still paused, and `--accept-challenge` refuses because an unused revision commit exists.
- `--accept-challenge` also refuses when a pinned file has been edited.
- A `resume` that ends paused now re-exports run-state.json and report.html, as `start` does, so the export shows the new base and attempt.

Worktrees may be at the base, at any revision commit already on the branch, or at the target. This covers a second interrupted resume that stacks a new revision on an earlier one while some worktrees are halfway between.
